notes_list.title: Pyrrole — Aromaticity and Basicity
notes_list.basic_overview: Pyrrole is a 6π aromatic heterocycle in which the nitrogen lone pair participates in aromaticity, making it much less basic than typical amines.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Protonating the nitrogen disrupts or competes with aromatic stabilization, so its basicity is low. Electrophilic substitution commonly occurs at C2.
notes_list.examples: Pyrrole vs pyridine is a classic comparison: pyrrole lone pair is aromatic; pyridine lone pair is not part of the aromatic sextet.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Mild electrophilic substitution conditions; strong acids can protonate or polymerize sensitive heterocycles.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Draw resonance contributors showing lone-pair donation into the ring; then compare availability of the lone pair for protonation.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Basicity depends on the free energy difference between neutral and protonated forms; aromaticity loss on protonation is a major factor.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not say “nitrogen always makes a ring basic”; pyrrole demonstrates the opposite.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
